dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.subtitle: Overview: services, corpora, recent index runs.
dashboard.explain_body:
Expert mode landing page. Check that PostgreSQL and Ollama answer, that the default generation model (qwen2.5:7b) is downloaded, and see ingested corpora + recent index runs.

Actions: refresh to reread live state, pull the default model if missing, open Adminer to inspect the DB by hand.

query.title: Retrieval
query.subtitle: Adjustable retrieval with fine filters and raw payload.
query.explain_body:
A detailed version of Chat, to inspect the retrieval.

What Chat doesn't do and this page does:
• Force a precise `index_run_id` instead of the most recent.
• Enable filters by document_id, file_name, path, tags, metadata.
• See the full JSON payload (chunks with score, rank, source_path, full chunk_text).
• Set top_k explicitly.

Use this page when you want to understand why a retrieval brings up a given chunk. For daily use, Chat is enough.
query.question: Question

playground.title: Prompt Playground
playground.subtitle: Ollama direct, without retrieval.
playground.explain_body:
Talk to the LLM **without** retrieving anything from your documents. No chunk is injected in the prompt.

Use cases:
• Test a model (qwen2.5:7b, llama3.2:3b...) on a general question, see what it knows by itself.
• Compare two system prompts on the same question.
• Tune hyperparameters (temperature, top_p, num_predict, num_ctx, seed).
• Verify a freshly pulled model answers correctly.

If you want the LLM to use your documents, use Chat or the Retrieval page.
playground.no_messages: No message yet. Send a prompt below.

ingest.subtitle: Path on the raglab server.

index.title: Indexing
index.subtitle: Chunking + embeddings + pgvector storage.
index.explain_body:
Step 2 after ingestion. Turns documents of a corpus into vectorised chunks, stored in pgvector, ready to be queried.

Each run creates an `index_run` with a precise combination (chunking strategy × embedding model × dimension). You can launch several runs on the same corpus to compare strategies (that's what benchmarks are for).

Parameters:
• Strategy — `traditional` (fixed window + overlap), `slide` (sliding window), `late` (chunks with upstream/downstream context).
• Embedding model — probed on first run to determine its real dimension.
• Incremental — reuses chunks/embeddings from a compatible previous run instead of recomputing everything.
index.incremental_checkbox: Reuse chunks/embeddings from the last compatible run
index.loading: indexing in progress (may take a while)…

graph_index.title: Graph indexing (Neo4j)
graph_index.subtitle: Vector-in-graph on Neo4j 5.
graph_index.explain_body:
Graph counterpart to vector indexing. Each chunk becomes a `(:Chunk)` Neo4j node carrying an `embedding_d{N}` property plus a `[:BELONGS_TO]` relation to its document and `[:FROM_RUN]` to the index run.

Goal: run the same query against pgvector vs Neo4j (Neo4j 5 vector index) with identical chunks and embeddings and compare retrieval quality.

Next phase (8.2): entity extraction (LLM or spaCy) will add typed nodes enabling hybrid retrieval: KNN seeds + graph traversal.
graph_index.neo4j_status_unreachable: Neo4j unreachable — run `docker compose up -d neo4j` and reload.
graph_index.extract_entities_hint: Creates typed `(:Entity)` nodes (Person, Location, Organization…) linked to chunks via `[:MENTIONS]`. Unlocks hybrid retrieval (KNN seed + graph traversal).
graph_index.extraction_engine_hint: LLM: qwen2.5:7b via Ollama, multilingual, slow (~2-5s/chunk). spaCy: fast (~50ms/chunk), needs the model pre-downloaded.

graph_query.title: Graph retrieval (Neo4j)
graph_query.subtitle: KNN over the Neo4j vector index.
graph_query.explain_body:
Graph counterpart to the Retrieval page. Fire a question against a Neo4j index and see the chunks ranked by the vector index, with the same filters as the pgvector side (corpus, file_name, source_path, tags).

Note: `metadata_equals` filters are not yet supported on the graph side (metadata is serialised as JSON). They'll come back when metadata becomes first-class nodes in phase 8.2, alongside a hybrid mode: KNN seed → `k`-hop expansion → re-rank.
graph_query.no_runs: No graph index run for this corpus. Go to Graph indexing to create one.
graph_query.mode_hint: Vector: pure KNN (same as pgvector). Hybrid: KNN seed + re-rank by shared entities. Needs a run indexed with entity extraction.
graph_query.seed_top_n_hint: How many vector hits act as seeds for collecting reference entities.
graph_query.entity_weight_hint: 0 = pure KNN, 1 = rank entirely on shared entities. Typical: 0.2 to 0.4.
graph_query.subgraph_hint: Show the network of retrieved chunks and the entities they mention, to visualise semantic links.
graph_query.subgraph_empty: No links in the retrieved chunks — run a query on chunks indexed with entities.

lexml.title: LexML Brasil
lexml.subtitle: Collect + ingest + index.
lexml.long_note: very long — leave the page open

lexml.fulltext_help: Collects the full text of federal laws (list: Senado open data API, text: planalto.gov.br), then has the local LLM write typed questions (paraphrase, article reference, acronym or proper noun). Each answer is a quote located in the document, so relevance is judged at passage level.

ollama.title: Ollama models
ollama.subtitle: Install, remove and list locally available LLM models.
ollama.explain_body:
LLM model management. Ollama stores each downloaded model in the Docker volume `raglab_ollama_data`.

• Status: verify the Ollama service answers and the default generation model (qwen2.5:7b) is installed.
• Models table: shows locally available ones, with size and date. Delete those you no longer need (mind the one flagged `default`).
• Pull: download a new model from ollama.com (type its exact name, e.g. `llama3.2:3b`, `nomic-embed-text`).

benchmarks.title: Benchmarks
benchmarks.subtitle: History of recall runs with comparable metrics.
benchmarks.no_runs: No benchmark recorded yet. Run `raglab experiment recall` or POST to `/api/experiments/recall`.
benchmarks.backend_hint: Which store to search — pgvector (PostgreSQL) or neo4j (vector-in-graph). "both" runs the same test against both sides for comparison.
benchmarks.ragas_hint: Computes faithfulness (grounded in the chunks?), answer_relevancy (does it answer the question?) and answer_correctness (matches the ground truth?).
benchmarks.ragas_hint_slow: ⚠ On: answers are generated, then graded in a second pass (3 judges per case).
benchmarks.chart_hint: Check a row to include it in the chart (max 5 runs)
benchmarks.chart_empty: Select at least one run to display the chart.
benchmarks.explain_body:
Each row is an evaluation run: (corpus, strategy) evaluated against a ground-truth dataset.

• Launch tab: pick an indexed corpus, a strategy, and a ground-truth dataset (auto-detected from data/benchmarks/*).
• History tab: select 2-5 rows to compare their metrics (Recall@K, MRR) visually in the chart.

Zeros usually mean the ground truth doesn't match the corpus (e.g. Wikipedia corpus with LexML ground truth).
benchmarks.dataset_mismatch: ⚠ The dataset may not match the corpus. Check that `expected_file_names` in the ground truth exist in the corpus.
benchmarks.no_dataset_detected: No dataset detected. Download one via Corpus → Benchmark dataset, or use LexML auto-gen.
benchmarks.custom_help: Write your own questions and what the RAG should retrieve. Useful to evaluate against your own documents.
benchmarks.custom_name_hint: Used as the directory under data/benchmarks/custom_<name>
benchmarks.custom_corpus_hint: Optional — pick a corpus to see the list of available files.
benchmarks.custom_file_hint: Pick from the corpus; the name is appended to the field below.
benchmarks.custom_file_names_hint: Comma-separated. At least one if no expected answer.
benchmarks.custom_answer_hint: Optional. Will be used later to measure faithfulness.
benchmarks.custom_saved: {{count}} cases saved in {{dir}}. Available in the Launch tab.
benchmarks.judge_hint: A judge from another model family avoids the model grading its own answers. llama.cpp must be reachable (RAGLAB_LLAMACPP_BASE_URL): the CLI starts it, the API does not.
benchmarks.ragas_limit_hint: Empty = all. Retrieval always covers every case.
benchmarks.rerank_hint: Adds the cross-encoder stage (pgvector). Its VRAM is freed before the RAGAS judge pass.

corpus_page.title: Corpus
corpus_page.subtitle: Feed the base: import a folder, download a benchmark, load LexML, manage.
corpus_page.explain_body:
A corpus is a bundle of documents stored in the base. Before any query, you need to ingest documents and then index them (Indexing page).

• Local folder: point to a server path containing .txt / .pdf / .docx.
• Benchmark dataset: download an open-source Q/A set (PIAF, FQuAD...) — produces an ingestible corpus + a ground truth for the Benchmarks page.
• LexML Brasil: all-in-one pipeline (collect + ingest + index) for the Brazilian legal corpus.
• Manage: delete an existing corpus (cascades to documents, chunks, index runs).
corpus_page.folder_help: Path must exist server-side (not your own machine if using Docker).
corpus_page.bench_help: Each loader produces `corpus/` + `ground_truth.jsonl` + `metadata.json`. After download, run the ingestion below.
corpus_page.bench_limit_hint: Number of questions sampled at random. The corpus stays complete: every passage of the dataset is written. Empty = all questions.
corpus_page.bench_seed_hint: Same seed = same questions, so benchmarks stay comparable across runs.
corpus_page.lexml_help: Collects legal records from lexml.gov.br, ingests and indexes in one pass.
corpus_page.manage_help: Deleting a corpus also removes its documents, chunks, index runs and embeddings.

edu.title: The pipeline, live
edu.subtitle: Ask a question: each stage lights up as it runs. Click a stage to learn what it does.
edu.diagram_label: RAG architecture diagram: from question to answer
edu.hint: Click a stage to see what it does, the code that runs it and the values of your question.
edu.replayed: This stage runs before the stream opens: its duration is real, its animation is replayed.
edu.from_timings: The API answered without streaming: the diagram is rebuilt from the response timings.
edu.vector_norm: Norm: {{norm}} (normalised embeddings have a norm close to 1).
edu.prompt_truncated: Truncated preview: the full prompt contains every passage.

question.name: Question
question.what: The text typed in the Chat, sent to the API with the chosen corpus and index. A legal citation (“art. 49 da Lei 8.078”) is spotted in it with regular expressions.
question.why: Everything starts here: the same question goes through every stage, and the diagram shows what each one does with it.

routing.name: Router
routing.what: Detects language and intent, picks the corpus, and may decline to answer when no document covers the question.
routing.why: Avoid searching in the wrong place and inventing an off-topic answer: abstaining beats hallucinating.
routing.disabled: The router is not enabled for this request: the question goes straight to the chosen corpus.

embed.name: Embedding
embed.what: An embedding model turns the question into a vector of numbers that encodes its meaning.
embed.why: Texts with similar meaning get close vectors: that is what makes search by meaning, not just by words, possible.
embed.disabled: No vector search for this request, hence no embedding.

retrieval.name: Vector search
retrieval.what: Compares the question vector with the indexed passages' vectors (pgvector, exact cosine distance by default) and keeps the closest.
retrieval.why: Find, in milliseconds and among thousands of passages, those about the topic even without the same words.
retrieval.disabled: Search is lexical only for this request.

lexical.name: BM25
lexical.what: Classic full-text search: scores passages by the exact words of the question and how rare they are.
lexical.why: Embeddings sometimes miss precise terms (article numbers, acronyms, proper names) that BM25 always finds.
lexical.disabled: Hybrid search disabled: only vector search is used.

fusion.name: Fusion
fusion.what: Merges the two rankings (vector and BM25) into one with Reciprocal Rank Fusion.
fusion.why: Get the strengths of both searches without comparing scores on different scales.
fusion.disabled: No fusion: only one search ran.

rerank.name: Re-ranking
rerank.what: A cross-encoder reads each (question, passage) pair and re-orders them precisely.
rerank.why: More accurate than search but too slow for the whole corpus: it only runs on the best candidates.
rerank.disabled: Re-ranking disabled: the search order is kept.

prompt.name: Prompt
prompt.what: Assembles the instructions, the question and the retrieved passages (with their rank) into the message sent to the LLM.
prompt.why: The prompt is what forces the model to answer only from the sources and to cite them [Rank X].
prompt.disabled: No generation requested: no prompt is built.

generation.name: LLM
generation.what: The language model (Ollama, llama.cpp or vLLM) reads the prompt and writes the answer, token by token.
generation.why: Turn raw passages into a clear, sourced answer; it is the most expensive stage in time and GPU.
generation.disabled: No generation requested for this request.

answer.name: Answer
answer.what: The answer shown in the Chat, with clickable citations to the sources.
answer.why: Every claim can be checked against the cited passage: that is what makes a RAG trustworthy.

citation.name: Law article reference
citation.what: Spots an article reference in the question (“art. 49 da Lei 8.078”, “article L. 221-18 du Code de la consommation”) with regular expressions.
citation.why: When an article is cited, searching the whole corpus drowns it among similar texts: the search is restricted to that text and the article goes first.
citation.disabled: Option off: the question is searched across the whole corpus.

edu.hint_selected: Click the active stage again to close its explanation.
edu.not_run_yet: Ask a question to see this stage's real values.

fig.space_label: The question and its nearest passages in the embedding space
fig.space_caption: Distance to the centre follows 1 − cosine (this request's values); the angles only spread the points.
fig.lexical_caption: BM25 score of each passage: term frequency, weighted by rarity and passage length.
fig.rrf_caption: Only ranks count (k = {{k}}, BM25 weight = {{weight}}): no need to compare a cosine with a BM25 score.
fig.rerank_caption: Each line joins a passage's position before and after the cross-encoder reread it.

route.title: The path of this question
route.title_planned: The planned path with the current options
route.citation_none: No article cited: the search covers the whole corpus.
route.citation_law: “{{label}}” recognised: search restricted to that text, article first.
route.citation_unknown_law: “{{label}}” recognised but not in the index: the search covers the whole corpus.
route.citation_off: Option off: the question is not analysed.
route.mode_dense: Vector: only the meaning-based search runs, BM25 is skipped.
route.mode_lexical: Keywords: only BM25 runs, the question is not embedded.
route.mode_hybrid: Hybrid: both searches run (one after the other, independently), then their rankings are fused with RRF.
route.rerank_on: On: the cross-encoder rereads the {{count}} best candidates and keeps the most relevant.
route.rerank_off: Off: the search order is kept as is.
route.rerank_skipped: Skipped: no GPU on the server (on CPU it would take several seconds).
route.rerank_cpu: On, running on CPU for lack of a GPU: slower than usual.

citation.what: Two regular expressions find a law and an article in the question
citation.law: the law number, with or without a dot (8.078 or 8078)
citation.parse: nothing cited: the search covers the whole corpus
citation.restrict: law found in the index: only that document is searched
citation.pin: the cited article's passages go first

embed.prefix: e5 models are trained with a prefix: “query: ” for a question
embed.encode: the model returns a vector (384 numbers for e5-small)
embed.passage: Indexed passages were embedded with the “passage: ” prefix

retrieval.what: Exact search for the passages closest to the question
retrieval.distance: <=> is pgvector's cosine distance (0 = same direction)
retrieval.run: only the passages of the chosen index

lexical.what: BM25 computed in PostgreSQL (ts_rank has no IDF)
lexical.idf: a word rare in the index (small df) weighs more
lexical.candidates: Candidates: passages containing at least one word of the question
lexical.tf: how many times the word appears in the passage
lexical.norm: long passages are penalised (b), repetition is capped (k1)
lexical.sum: score = sum over the question's words

fusion.what: Reciprocal Rank Fusion: only ranks count, not scores
fusion.dense: ranked well by the vector search: it scores
fusion.lexical: ranked well by BM25 too: it scores again
fusion.absent: missing from a list: that list adds nothing

rerank.what: The cross-encoder reads the question and the passage together
rerank.sort: Sort by score; ties keep the search order

prompt.what: Each passage is numbered by its rank in the message sent to the model
prompt.rank: the model cites this number: [Rank N]
prompt.rules: The instructions: answer only from these excerpts, cite [Rank N]

generation.what: Streaming call to the model: the answer arrives piece by piece
generation.stream: stream: True, the server sends each token as soon as it is produced
generation.temperature: low temperature: factual answers, little invention
generation.token: each piece becomes an SSE “token” event in the Chat

answer.what: In the browser, every [Rank N] of the answer is found
answer.click: and turned into a clickable chip pointing to source N

retrieval.mode_hint: dense = embedding similarity, lexical = BM25 on words, hybrid = fusion of both (RRF).
retrieval.lexical_weight_hint: 0 = dense order only, 1 = BM25 order only, 0.5 = plain RRF.
retrieval.rrf_k_hint: The smaller k, the more top ranks weigh. Default 60.
retrieval.rerank_hint: Retrieval returns {{candidates}} candidates; {{model}} reads each with the question and keeps the top-k.
retrieval.rerank_stats: Re-ranking: {{candidates}} candidates, {{scored}} pairs scored, {{hits}} read from the cache (cumulative hit rate {{rate}}%)
retrieval.citations_hint: A reference in the question (“art. 49 da Lei 8.078”, “article L. 221-18 du Code de la consommation”) limits the search to that text and puts the article first.
retrieval.citation_badge_title: Pinned: the question cites this passage's law and article.
retrieval.citation_unresolved: Citation recognised ({{label}}) but the law is not in the index: normal search.
retrieval.rerank_notice_skipped_no_gpu: Re-ranking skipped: no GPU available (it would take several seconds on CPU). Force it with “on” if needed.
retrieval.rerank_notice_cpu: Re-ranking ran on CPU, without a GPU: expect several seconds per query.

graph.title: Citation graph
graph.subtitle: Laws, articles and references in Neo4j.
graph.explain_body:
A classic RAG finds the article that looks like the question, not the one it refers to ("nos termos do art. 12"). For each index run, raglab builds a structured graph in Neo4j from the chunks already stored: documents, sections, chunks (`PART_OF`, `NEXT`) and, for laws, `Law`, `Article`, `CITES`, `AMENDS`, `REVOKES`, extracted by rules, without an LLM.

PostgreSQL remains the source of chunks and vectors; Neo4j only holds the structure. The graph is built at indexing time when Neo4j answers, or with the button below (`raglab graph build`). See docs/graphe.md.
graph.neo4j_unreachable: Neo4j does not answer: `docker compose up -d neo4j`, then reload.
graph.search_placeholder: Number or word of the title
graph.build_first: Build this index run's graph to explore its laws.
graph.isolated: {{count}} articles without references are not drawn.
graph.click_hint: Click a node to see its references and the passage that carries them.
graph.cypher_hint: The same view in Cypher, to paste into
graph.entity_disabled_body: The Neo4j store with LLM-extracted entities (phase 8) was never measured; the citation graph replaces it. To turn it back on: RAGLAB_ENTITY_GRAPH_ENABLED=true.
graph.counts_summary: {{articles}} articles, {{cites}} article-to-article references — counts by type
